title: Holding Out for a Hero — symbolic soundtrack for the Ra -> Sobek retrieval call

media.lyrics_storage_rule: Full lyrics are not duplicated in this registry object; only short motif labels and paraphrases are retained.

interpretive_frame.user_request: Render the song as a modern soundtrack-like call from Ra to Sobek during the search for Horus's missing hands/arms.
interpretive_frame.canonical_scientific_label: Ra-coordinated Sobek retrieval mission in CT158/BD113
interpretive_frame.ancient_source_boundary: CT158/BD113 is the historical witness. The Bonnie Tyler song is a modern cultural overlay only.

stage_1_absence.song_motif: The song opens by asking where the capable men and gods have gone.
stage_1_absence.mission_rendering: A crisis exists because the required agent is not yet present.
stage_1_absence.ra_role: Ra is the authority who recognizes that a specialist must be brought in.
stage_1_absence.sobek_role: Sobek is the summoned retrieval specialist, not the missing victim.

stage_2_requirement.song_motif: The desired hero must be strong, fast, certain and ready after conflict.
stage_2_requirement.mission_rendering: The call is not for a passive witness but for an operator capable of entering a dangerous environment and returning with the target.
stage_2_requirement.sobek_fit: Symbolically fits Sobek's role as a powerful marsh/water deity assigned to search and recover the lost parts.

stage_3_target_question.song_motif: The song repeatedly defines what kind of rescuer is needed before the rescue occurs.
stage_3_target_question.critical_note: Sobek does not literally say the word 'Who?' in the UCL translation. WHO/WHAT is the JANUS analytical target-resolution question, answered by the surrounding CT158/BD113 lines.

stage_4_environment.mission_rendering: The hero is imagined as approaching through an elemental, dangerous environment.
stage_4_environment.ancient_parallel: Sobek's mission is explicitly aquatic: search at the banks of the water / marsh-fish setting.
stage_4_environment.boundary: The song's storm imagery is not evidence for a storm in CT158/BD113. This is atmospheric resonance only.

stage_5_remote_contact.song_motif: Someone beyond reach reaches back; another line evokes a distant watcher.
stage_5_remote_contact.mission_rendering: The absent/rescuing agent is first perceived at a distance, then approaches.
stage_5_remote_contact.registry_bridge: This creates a modern symbolic cross-reference to the existing Eye In The Sky line, but no historical or authorial connection is claimed.

stage_6_approach.song_motif: The approach is felt before arrival and is compared with heat/fire in the body.
stage_6_approach.mission_rendering: The rescue shifts from waiting to imminent intervention.
stage_6_approach.sobek_parallel: In the JANUS rendering this marks Sobek moving from summoned agent to active search/recovery agent.

stage_7_recovery.ancient_text_not_song: Sobek searches, identifies the location of the scattered parts and catches them with a snare/fish-trap; the target is resolved as Horus's hands/arms.
stage_7_recovery.soundtrack_function: The chorus supplies emotional momentum for the retrieval mission, not factual content.

stage_8_restoration.ancient_text_not_song: Horus's mother is credited with making the recovered hands/arms grow in their place.
stage_8_restoration.important_distinction: Sobek retrieves; he is not the final regrowth agent.

compact_cinematic_rendering_ru.label: MODERN_SOUNDTRACK_RENDERING_NOT_ANCIENT_QUOTE
compact_cinematic_rendering_ru.text: Ра фиксирует потерю и зовёт того, кто способен пройти туда, где остальные не справились. JANUS сначала задаёт главный вопрос миссии: КОГО / ЧТО ИЩЕМ? Текст отвечает: руки и предплечья Хора. Затем второй вопрос: ГДЕ? У воды, там, где они были рассеяны. Третий: КАК? Собек идёт искать как владыка болот, локализует цель и извлекает её ловушкой. Но миссия Собека заканчивается возвращением утраченного: окончательное восстановление — рост рук на их месте — приписано матери Хора. Песня работает здесь как современный саундтрек ожидания сильного спасателя, который должен прийти через опасную стихию и вернуть то, что было утрачено.

motif_matrix.warning: Do not back-project song weather into the ancient text.

why_it_fits_the_registry_line: The song is built around absence, urgent need, selection of a capable rescuer, dangerous elemental imagery, approach and hoped-for intervention.
CT158/BD113 contains a real ancient retrieval mission with distinct authority, search agent, target, place, method and recovery outcome.
Therefore the song works well as a modern emotional soundtrack to the mission architecture without changing the evidence model.
The strongest structural parallel is CALL -> SPECIALIST -> DANGEROUS ENVIRONMENT -> APPROACH -> RECOVERY, not any claim that Bonnie Tyler's song encodes Egyptian mythology.
highest_admissible_claim: Holding Out for a Hero is an effective modern soundtrack for the JANUS Ra-to-Sobek retrieval rendering because its central dramatic structure is the urgent call for a powerful rescuer who must arrive through danger and overcome rising odds. The ancient evidence remains CT158/BD113: Ra commissions Sobek to search for the scattered hands/arms of Horus near the water; Sobek retrieves them; Horus's mother is credited with regrowth. The song contributes emotional and symbolic framing only.
